findings.title: Patchstack vulnerability database entry and advisory timeline for Elementor CSRF (CVE-2026-62062)
findings.summary_md: Patchstack published the vulnerability entry on 25 September 2026, assigning CVE-2026-62062 (CVSS 8.8) to the Elementor Website Builder plugin CSRF affecting versions 4.3.0 and 4.3.1. The entry records researcher Saggre's original disclosure to Patchstack on 22 September 2026, the vendor fix in version 4.3.2 released on 24 September 2026, and the public advisory release on 25 September 2026.

findings.title: Patchstack security advisory article: Cross-Site Request Forgery in Elementor Plugin Affecting 2 Million+ Sites
findings.summary_md: Patchstack's public advisory, released 25 September 2026, details the CSRF mechanism in Elementor's Editor Events module: the raw REQUEST_URI check for the literal string elementor/v1/events/ bypasses WordPress REST nonce validation. The advisory confirms versions 4.3.0 and 4.3.1 are affected, that Patchstack received the report from researcher Saggre on 22 September, and that Elementor fixed it in 4.3.2 by reading the resolved REST route instead of the raw URI.

findings.title: Elementor changelog: releases 4.3.0 (2026-09-22) and 4.3.1 (2026-09-23)
findings.summary_md: The Elementor changelog records the release of plugin versions 4.3.0 on 22 September 2026 (introducing the Editor Events module and other features) and 4.3.1 on 23 September 2026. The timeline from Patchstack confirms the security fix was delivered in version 4.3.2 on 24 September 2026, meaning the vulnerable releases existed for roughly one to two days before the patch.

findings.title: BleepingComputer coverage of Elementor CSRF vulnerability
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer published its report on 25 September 2026 at 02:13 PM (likely US time, making it potentially concurrent with or shortly before the story's 18:13 UTC first_seen). The article covers the same CSRF mechanism described by Patchstack, notes the 10 million active installations and up to 2 million sites running the vulnerable 4.3.0 and 4.3.1 versions, and confirms the fix in 4.3.2. It explicitly references Patchstack's analysis and links to the Patchstack advisory article.
